name: armstrong-2002-v1
description:
From original source:
-----

The authors showed that clustering algorithms reveal that lymphoblastic  leukemias with MLL translocations (MLL) can clearly be separated from conventional acute lymphoblastic (ALL) and acute myelogenous leukemias (AML).

From these, we formed two data sets with the following distribution of samples:
Armstrong-V1: 24 ALL and 48 MLL
Armstrong-V2: 24 ALL, 20 MLL and 28 AML

Parameters used in our filter:
Armstrong-V1: l= 3 and c=30
Armstrong-V2: l= 3 and c=18
creator: Scott A Armstrong et al.
citation: Armstrong, Scott A, Jane E Staunton, Lewis B Silverman, Rob Pieters, Monique L den Boer, Mark D Minden, Stephen E Sallan, Eric S Lander, Todd R Golub, and Stanley J Korsmeyer. "MLL Translocations Specify a Distinct Gene Expression Profile That Distinguishes a Unique Leukemia." Nature Genetics 30, no. 1 (January 2002): 41-47.
